title: Playbook v1
description: Versioned, machine-checkable workflow template. A playbook compiles into a durable plan; it never carries concrete provider/model names — only a step contract (executor_role + minimum_model_level + context_budget) resolved by the runtime ladder. See issue #1372.

when_to_use.description: One-to-two sentences «когда предлагать этот плейбук», in the user's language. Optional in the schema so already-saved playbooks stay valid; required for a profile-scope save (issue #1851). The runner injects it into the profile's system prompt so the playbook is reachable from a plain request without the id; playbook_check_reachability treats a non-empty value as route P.

requires.description: What the playbook needs from a profile: skill-catalog sections that must be enabled and MCP tools it calls. Checked by scripts/check-playbook-reachability.mjs and the playbook_check_reachability tool (issue #1756).

inputs.description: Run values the step texts rely on as {name} placeholders (e.g. the target repository of an engineering playbook). A required input that playbook_run vars do not carry and that cannot be derived from the goal is a compile error — a plan is never created with a literal {name} in its steps (issue #1725).

derive.description: github_repo: owner/name of the single GitHub repository the goal links to.

step_type.description: Id of the typed step in the playbook repo's step library (e.g. define-use-case, sandbox, archive). Informational: the library's sub-steps are already rendered into instructions.

already_done.description: Deterministic pre-check (issue #1959): the engine evaluates these registry validators when the step is claimed, BEFORE any model run. All pass → the step is closed with an audit row (evidence {already_done:true}) and the next step is taken with zero model runs; not pass → the normal run. Keys are the same registry validators as `validation` (pr_opened, ci_green, file_exists, …).

wait.description: Durable wait (programmatic steps only): poll this step's own validation every poll_every_sec, without spending attempts, until it passes. On timeout_sec the step does NOT fail — it escalates to the owner and keeps waiting (issue #1959); a validator may mark a fail as final to wake at once (e.g. a closed-unmerged PR).
